Plaster Stadium TV: CBS Sports Network | Watch Live RADIO: KSU Owl Network | Listen: KSU Owls App, Tune In | Online: KSUOwls.com | Satellite: SiriusXM 261 Team Info: Game Notes/Depth Charts | Clippings | 2026 Football Media Guide • Kennesaw State football looks to get back on track and even its Conference USA record when it heads to Springfield, Missouri for the second time in program history to take on Missouri State on Wednesday, Oct. 14 at Robert W. Plaster Stadium. • The Owls are coming off back-to-back heartbreaking one-score losses, falling 17-14 to Arkansas State and 27-26 to Jax State. The Bears have lost three-straight entering Wednesday, including a 34-13 defeat to WKU last week. • In its CUSA opener last week, Kennesaw State looked as good as it has offensively all season, recording the eighth-most FBS offensive yards in program history (411) and seventh-most passing yards (293) in a single game. • After averaging just 87 rushing yards against Georgia State and Tennessee, the Owls have found another gear, averaging 157 yards per game over their last two weeks. • Through five games, Kennesaw State ranks fourth in CUSA in points allowed (23.4), but has allowed just 18.8 points per game against non-Power 4 opponents. • Kennesaw State is the only CUSA team with four players who have rushed for at least 100 yards and a score in 2026 and one of only 20 teams in FBS. • Kennesaw State has scored at least 24 points in nine-straight regular-season conference games. • Sr. WR Brayden Munroe recorded the second-most receiving yards in program history last week against Jax State, hauling in seven catches for 159 yards -- second-most of any receiver in CUSA this season. • Munroe leads the team with 299 receiving yards on 19 catches, ranking sixth in the league with 59.8 receiving yards per game. • r-So. LB Tywon Christopher had a career night as well last week, recording 15 tackles, 2.0 tackles for loss and a forced fumble. He is one of only two players in FBS this season to record those numbers in a single game. • Kennesaw State has created havoc for teams this season, ranking second in the conference with seven turnovers gained (five fumble recoveries and two interceptions), and ranking 10th nationally (first in CUSA) with the five fumble recoveries. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect College Football News Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings Brad Crawford and Chris Hummer are back with their weekly picks and predictions for the weekend's best games Getty Images The Week 7 schedule features six top-25 matchups, giving contenders ample opportunity to strengthen their playoff cases before next month's first selection committee rankings . Nearing the midway point, preseason expectations now carry little weight -- ask teams like LSU, Texas &M, Michigan and Penn State -- with narratives already materializing. We're picking several of Saturday's showdowns that come with playoff implications, raising the stakes for teams in the SEC, Big Ten and Big 12 trying to protect unbeaten records . Ohio State-Indiana, Notre Dame-BYU, Alabama-Tennessee -- good luck finding a quiet window on this slate. Season results : Brad Crawford (38-13 straight up, 29-21-1 ATS); Chris Hummer (40-11 straight up, 27–23-1 ATS) We're coming off my personal worst picks week of my career straight up (3-5, yuck!) after a bevy of upsets I didn't see coming. The against-the-spread total wasn't fatal, at least. Hummer has narrowed the gap to two games back ATS and has assumed the lead straight up after a terrific showing. If these picks aren't enough this week, head to our CBS Sports expert picks page where Hummer's on a heater. No. 16 Mississippi State at No. 22 LSU (-10.5) Hummer ( LSU -10.5) : This game sets up for a LSU bounce back. Even if Kamario Taylor were healthy -- and his status is in doubt this week -- the Tigers have a lot of advantages in this game, including an elite secondary and pass rush. The big question for LSU is whether Sam Leavitt can avoid turnovers. If he plays clean, which has been a problem all year given that he leads the nation in INTs, LSU should roll. … LSU 38, Mississippi State 24. Crawford (LSU -10.5) : Is this the week LSU finally puts it together against an opponent of substance? It is time the Tigers look the part as a potential CFP team after two SEC losses already. A third ends any hope of getting to the 12-team bracket, even if LSU wins out from there and finishes 9-3. The resume simply won't be good enough to warrant enough attention. I'm giving this the must-win label for Lane Kiffin, whose first season is teetering on total disappointment if he's handed a third loss before playing Alabama in November. ... LSU 37, Mississippi State 20. Florida at No. 7 Texas (-9.5) Hummer ( Florida +9.5) : Which version of Arch Manning and the Texas passing attack are we going to get? That's going to determine whether Texas rolls in this game. The Gators have the worst pass defense in the SEC and have been torched by far less talented (on paper) passing attacks than Texas. But Texas has been incredibly inconsistent on offense this year, ranking just 62nd nationally in passing yards per game. Texas, a top-15 rushing defense, is set up to contain Jadan Baugh and Florida's rushing attack. But can it score enough to cover in this one? I'm extremely skeptical. Perhaps Texas responds and blows Florida out -- a real possibility -- but that's just not the team we've seen this year. … Texas 31, Florida 24. Crawford (Texas -9.5) : I'm not positive on this, but the public play will assuredly be Florida, given the potential hangover effect from the Longhorns' loss to Oklahoma . The Gators stink worse, though, with consecutive blowout losses in SEC play since starting the season 4-0 and ranked No. 8. Florida's secondary looks atrocious after being carved up by LaNorris Sellers last week and Arch Manning could do the same. Manning has been off more than sharp this fall, but this is a matchup I like for the Texas offense. The Longhorns lost to Florida last season, and that could play a role in Saturday's performance, too. ... Texas 34, Florida 24. No. 6 Alabama (-6.5) at No. 14 Tennessee Hummer (Alabama -6.5) : The Vols have survived this year behind an elite defense. That unit has carried an offense that ranks just 66th nationally in yards per play and 110th in passing yards per game. But is that defense good enough to hold off Alabama? I'm highly skeptical. Alabama's defense has been susceptible in the secondary this year. But the Vols don't have the passing offense to take advantage of that. The Crimson Tide roll in this game for a second straight year. … Alabama 24, Tennessee 17. Crawford (Alabama -6.5) : It almost feels disrespectful to call this a "get-right" game for the Crimson Tide given their recent struggles at Neyland Stadium, but unless DeSean Bishop controls this game on the ground for the Vols, I don't see a path to a Tennessee victory. The passing game is a struggle for Josh Heupel, and Alabama can score points in a hurry. Falling behind in the first half could lead to a chorus of boos in Knoxville if the Crimson Tide's defense can put together stops. This is a dangerous game for Tennessee, not so much the betting favorites even without Ryan Coleman-Williams on the outside. ... Alabama 30, Tennessee 17. No. 13 Missouri at No. 9 Ole Miss (-6.5) Hummer ( Missouri +6.5) : Ole Miss should have a detailed scouting report on Austin Simmons in this one given that Pete Golding faced him every day for years at Ole Miss. This game will tell us a lot about whether the Rebels' secondary is really any better after their blowout loss to Florida. Missouri is an excellent team. The Tigers are stout up front defensively and have a passing attack that can expose Ole Miss' defense. This game has a ton of star power crossover -- Kewan Lacy went from Missouri to Ole Miss, Simmons from Oxford to Columbia -- and I think it is close throughout. … Ole Miss 31, Missouri 28. Crawford (Missouri +6.5) : Is there anyone out there who saw this being a top-15 matchup a month ago? The Tigers' run without Ahmad Hardy has really been impressive. Jamal Roberts has back-to-back 200-yard outings on the ground and could easily have a third against a defense that's had its issues this season. I like Missouri in this spot with the points. I'm still not sure what to make of the Rebels outside of Trinidad Chambliss . You know what you're getting out of him, but Kewan Lacy is banged up and play on the other side of the football has left much to be desired. ... Ole Miss 30, Missouri 24. No. 18 Oklahoma State at No. 20 Houston (-3.5) Hummer ( Oklahoma State +3.5) : The Cowboys have gotten better every week this season to the point where, with their offense, you can really start to imagine them as an immediate Big 12 title threat. But this is by far their in Big 12 play. Houston is among the nation's best rushing attacks, and Oklahoma State is among the least successful run defenses in the country on a down-to-down basis. Houston plays more zone coverage than any other Big 12 team to prevent big plays. Houston's secondary hasn't succeeded in that area, given the Cougars' rank of 126th nationally in passes allowed of 20-plus yards. This game will come down to two areas: 1. Can Houston control the clock and convert in the red zone? 2. Can Oklahoma State create chunk plays in the passing game? I'm not willing to pick the outright upset here, but I think the Cowboys are in position to have a lot of offensive success in this one. … Houston 31, Oklahoma State 28. Crawford (Oklahoma State +3.5) : Oklahoma State's path to an upset starts with explosive plays while trying to keep Conner Weigman contained on the other side of the football. The Cowboys don't need to dominate every snap if they're turning opportunities into chunk plays and touchdowns. Force Houston to chase points, and suddenly the pressure shifts to the favorite at home in front of what Willie Fritz hopes will be a sellout crowd. This is a matchup with significant Big 12 title game implications, especially since the Cougars already have a loss in conference play at Texas Tech . ... Oklahoma State 34, Houston 31. Penn State at Michigan (-5.5) Hummer (Michigan -5.5) : The losing coach in this one is going to be feeling very uncomfortable. If Penn State falls, it'll be four straight dropped games. If Michigan loses, the Wolverines will have lost three in a row and will be out of the playoff hunt before the calendar turns to November. Michigan will have to run to win in this one. The Nittany Lions have an excellent secondary and, to be kind, Michigan's passing attack has been far from a strength. The good news for the Wolverines is that the Nittany Lions rank 113th nationally in yards allowed per carry. Coming out of a bye -- and given Penn State's struggles to run the football -- I like the Wolverines to cover. … Michigan 27, Penn State 21. Crawford (Penn State +5.5) : Neither of these teams has won a game in the Big Ten, and it's mid-October. That's unacceptable for two first-year staffs at these respective blueblood programs. picks.blurb: Ohio State @ Indiana Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers' Ohtani dilemma NFL hot seats Champions League updates Heisman Watch Ohio State @ Indiana Preview And Prediction Indiana Hoosiers linebacker Isaiah Jones (46) works to bring down Ohio State Buckeyes quarterback Julian Sayin (10) on Saturday, Dec. 6, 2025, during the Big Ten football championship at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 6:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 4 Ohio State travels to No. 5 Indiana for a massive Big Noon showdown. Can the Buckeyes avenge last year's Big Ten Championship loss? One of the biggest games of the college football season is set for Saturday afternoon as No. 4 Ohio State travels to Bloomington to take on No. 5 Indiana in FOX's Big Noon Saturday showdown. And there is plenty of bad blood between these two programs. The last time these teams met, Indiana stunned Ohio State 13-10 in the 2025 Big Ten Championship Game, ending the Buckeyes' undefeated season. Now, Ryan Day and Ohio State have an opportunity to return the favor against Curt Cignetti's defending national champions. Ohio State enters at 5-1, while Indiana remains undefeated at 6-0. Both teams are 3-0 in Big Ten play, making this matchup potentially decisive in the conference championship race. Ohio State: Can Julian Sayin Deliver? Ohio State's offense has been explosive this season, averaging more than 42 points per game. Quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown for approximately 1,772 yards, while superstar wide receiver Jeremiah Smith has been nearly unstoppable, recording 48 receptions for 916 yards and 11 touchdowns. Smith is the most dangerous player in college football, and Indiana's secondary will have its hands full trying to contain him. However, last year's championship game exposed some serious problems for Ohio State. Sayin threw for 258 yards, and Smith recorded eight catches for 144 yards, but the Buckeyes managed just 10 points. Sayin was also sacked five times. Indiana's defensive front remains dangerous, averaging 3.3 sacks and 8.2 tackles for loss per game this season. Running back Bo Jackson, who has rushed for approximately 460 yards, must help establish balance and prevent Indiana from focusing entirely on Sayin. Indiana: The Hoosiers Aren't Going Anywhere Indiana might have lost Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza, but Curt Cignetti has kept the Hoosiers rolling. TCU transfer Josh Hoover has thrown for more than 1,300 yards with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions, while running back Turbo Richard has rushed for nearly 600 yards. Wide receiver Charlie Becker has also been outstanding, recording 529 receiving yards and eight touchdowns. Michigan State transfer Nick Marsh gives Indiana another dangerous weapon on the outside. Defensively, Indiana is allowing approximately 12 points per game and has demonstrated an ability to create pressure without sacrificing coverage. However, the Hoosiers haven't exactly dominated their recent competition. Indiana narrowly escaped Northwestern 29-23 before defeating Nebraska 20-17 last weekend. Those performances raise questions about whether the Hoosiers can consistently move the football against an elite opponent. Expect another physical, defensive battle between two legitimate College Football Playoff contenders. Indiana's defense will create problems for Sayin, and the Hoosiers should find success moving the football through Hoover and Richard. However, Ohio State has something Indiana doesn't: Jeremiah Smith. I expect Smith to deliver a massive performance, surpassing 100 receiving yards and making the difference in a game that comes down to the final possession. Sayin will make a few mistakes under pressure, but the Buckeyes' defense will get enough stops to escape Bloomington with a huge victory. Final Score: No. 4 Ohio State 24, No. 5 Indiana 20 Ohio State gets its revenge, hands Indiana its first loss of the season, and puts itself in an excellent position in the Big Ten championship race. The Ohio State Buckeyes are 4-1 and have a chance to pick up win No. 5 when Maryland comes to town in Week 6 of the college football season. Kickoff is set for 4:15 p.m. ET on Saturday in Columbus, which is an unusual time slot for a Buckeyes home game. Ohio State is a 34.5-point favorite at the time of this article. This matchup against Maryland should give the Buckeyes a chance to rotate through much of their depth ahead of a crucial game next week against the Indiana Hoosiers. I believe this is the last game where we're going to see Ohio State play its second- and third-string players for a significant amount of time. Ohio State vs Maryland score prediction for Week 6 Ahead of this matchup between the Terrapins and the Buckeyes, it's time for my weekly score prediction. I have Ohio State taking care of business by a score of 48-10 . I think the Buckeyes build a big lead in the first half and put the game away in the third quarter. Maryland gets a field goal in the first half and a touchdown in the second half for its only points of the day. A key storyline on the Maryland side is quarterback Malik Washington. Washington is a player Ohio State recruited, and the 6-foot-5 quarterback from the Maryland area was a highly talented prospect coming out of high school. However, turnovers have been a problem for him this season. Washington has thrown six interceptions over the last two games alone. That gives the Ohio State defense a real chance at forcing some turnovers on Saturday. Buckeyes need to keep the run game going against Maryland Ohio State needs to continue to establish a run game in this one. Both Bo Jackson and Ja'Kobi Jackson should have a chance for good days against a Maryland defense that allows 136.6 rushing yards per game. The Terrapins also give up 30 points per game, which ranks 115th in college football. This isn't a very good defense, and the Buckeyes should be able to put up points without much trouble. Of course, you're going to get a heavy dose of Jeremiah Smith in the first half. Expect Smith and QB Julian Sayin to connect for at least one touchdown. I wouldn't be surprised if Smith goes for 125 yards and makes it look easy before heading to the sideline after three quarters. Ohio State's run defense needs another strong showing On the other side of the ball, Maryland's run game is led by Iverson Howard. The Buckeyes stopped the run against Iowa last week, and they need to show that again against the Terrapins. Holding the Maryland ground game in check would put even more pressure on Washington to make plays through the air. Given his recent turnover issues, that's a spot where the Ohio State secondary can take advantage. Overall, I expect Ohio State to dominate its way to an easy win on Saturday. All eyes will be on Indiana next week in a big road test, where the Buckeyes will try to get their get-back after losing to the Hoosiers in the Big Ten Championship last season. (Photo by Ben Jackson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cole VanWiechen Wed, October 14, 2026 at 9:01 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads This is the one Ohio State fans have had circled since December. No. 4 Ohio State travels to No. 5 Indiana on Saturday at noon ET on FOX for a rematch of last year's 13-10 Big Ten title game loss in Indianapolis. The Buckeyes are 3.5-point favorites, but going into Bloomington against the defending national champions is about as tough a road test as there is in the Big Ten. What to know about Indiana's offense Indiana looks a little different than last year, but they're still very good. The Hoosiers rank 20th nationally at 462.7 yards per game and average 40.2 points per game, also inside the top 20. They're balanced too, averaging 241 passing yards and 221 rushing yards a game. Josh Hoover has been excellent since transferring in from TCU. He's completing about 70% of his passes with 17 touchdowns and zero interceptions. That's a huge change for a quarterback whose biggest knock coming in was that he was interception prone. That says a lot about Curt Cignetti's coaching staff. The backfield is a two-headed monster in Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr., who both have over 550 rushing yards. Richard is averaging 8.4 yards per carry. The receiver room is just as dangerous. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh both have 30 catches for 530 yards. Becker has eight touchdowns and Marsh has six, and it's hard to find a better receiver duo in the Big Ten. What to know about Indiana's defense The defense might be even better. Indiana is allowing just 11.8 points per game, fifth in the country, and 237.8 yards per game, fourth nationally. The Hoosiers also haven't lost the turnover battle in a single game this season. The pass rush is led by Tobi Osunsami and Stephen Daley, who each have five sacks. Isaiah Jones and Rojiah Hardy are a strong linebacker duo in the middle. This is a complete, well-coached defense that won't give Ohio State much for free. Most important matchups Osunsami and Daley vs. Ohio State's offensive tackles . This might be the biggest matchup of the game. Phillip Daniels' status is still worth watching, and whoever starts at the other tackle spot has to hold up against two edge rushers with five sacks apiece. If Indiana can get to Julian Sayin, it changes everything. Devin Sanchez and Jermaine Mathews Jr. vs. Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh . Ohio State's corners just had their best combined game of the season against Maryland. Becker and Marsh are a completely different level of challenge, and Becker made two of the biggest catches against Mathews in last year's title game. Julian Sayin vs. a good team . Last year against Indiana, Sayin went 21-of-29 for 258 yards with a touchdown and an interception. He was solid, but Ohio State needed more. Sayin is coming off a sloppy game against Maryland, and this is his chance to show he can be the difference in a game like this.

picks.headline: ESPN FPI Predicts Tight Finish Between Indiana and Ohio State In Top-Five Clash
picks.blurb: ESPN FPI Predicts Tight Finish Between Indiana and Ohio State In Top-Five Clash - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers' Ohtani dilemma NFL hot seats Champions League updates Heisman Watch ESPN FPI Predicts Tight Finish Between Indiana and Ohio State In Top-Five Clash Oct 10, 2026; Lincoln, Nebraska, USA; Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti looks on during a timeout against the Nebraska Cornhuskers during the second quarter at Memorial Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dylan Widger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Zach Browning Mon, October 12, 2026 at 10:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Indiana's narrow 20-17 victory over Nebraska kept the Hoosiers undefeated, but ESPN's computers still give Ohio State the slightest of advantages heading into Saturday's top-five showdown at Memorial Stadium. The No. 5 Hoosiers (6-0) welcome the No. 4 Buckeyes (5-1) to Bloomington for a noon kickoff on FOX, with ESPN's Football Power Index projecting a game that could go either way. ESPN FPI gives Ohio State a narrow edge ESPN's latest FPI rankings have Ohio State at No. 3 nationally and Indiana at No. 7, but the gap between the two nearly disappears when accounting for Saturday's matchup in Bloomington. The model gives Ohio State a 52.2% chance of winning, with a projected margin of just 0.7 points. The Buckeyes are also 3.5-point favorites according to Monday's betting lines. ESPN's SP+ model sees an even closer contest, projecting a 26.4-26.2 Ohio State victory and giving the Buckeyes a 51% chance of winning. Essentially, the computers see a toss-up. That's a notable shift from the preseason, when the FPI gave Indiana just a 39.2% chance of defeating Ohio State. The Hoosiers have since improved those odds to 47.8%, reflecting how closely the two teams are viewed entering Saturday. What the projections mean for Indiana Ohio State presents Indiana with its toughest challenge of the season, particularly on offense. The Buckeyes are averaging 42.7 points per game, while quarterback Julian Sayin has thrown 17 touchdowns against just two interceptions. Then there's Jeremiah Smith, who may be college football's best player. But Indiana has its own reasons for confidence. The Hoosiers have won 22 consecutive games, including last December's 13-10 victory over Ohio State in the Big Ten Championship Game. Indiana has also yet to lose at Memorial Stadium under Curt Cignetti. And despite needing a fourth-quarter comeback to escape Nebraska, Indiana has repeatedly demonstrated an ability to win games that don't go according to plan. Indiana's offense struggled to establish its ground game against Nebraska, finishing with just 66 rushing yards on 22 attempts. That's a concerning number heading into a matchup with an Ohio State defense allowing 13.2 points per game. The Hoosiers likely won't be able to afford another similarly one-dimensional offensive performance against the Buckeyes. Still, with the game in Bloomington and both teams among the nation's best, the difference between victory and defeat could come down to a handful of plays. Can Arch Manning silence his critics and save the Longhorns' season? No. 7 Texas (4-1) returns home Saturday afternoon to face Florida (4-2) in a massive SEC matchup between two programs desperate for a bounce-back victory. The Longhorns are coming off an embarrassing 27-24 loss to Oklahoma, while Florida was dominated 38-19 at home by South Carolina. Both teams entered the season with championship aspirations, but another loss could seriously damage their College Football Playoff hopes. And for Texas quarterback Arch Manning, the pressure has never been higher. Texas: It's Time for Arch Manning to Deliver Manning entered the season as one of the Heisman Trophy favorites, but his performances have been anything but consistent. Through five games, Manning has thrown for 1,122 yards, 10 touchdowns, and five interceptions. Against Oklahoma, he completed 19 of 31 passes for 260 yards and three touchdowns, but two costly fourth-quarter interceptions helped the Sooners erase a 17-7 halftime deficit. The Longhorns are averaging just 379.2 yards per game, ranking 79th nationally. That's simply unacceptable considering the offensive talent Steve Sarkisian has assembled. However, Saturday presents an excellent opportunity to get things back on track. Florida's defense is allowing 393 yards and 29 points per game, including an alarming 268.7 passing yards per contest. Wide receiver Cam Coleman, who has 318 receiving yards and five touchdowns, should have opportunities to create explosive plays against a struggling Gators secondary. Defensively, Texas has been outstanding, allowing just 16 points and 96 rushing yards per game. Edge rusher Colin Simmons has been nearly unstoppable, recording 9.5 sacks. Florida: Can Jadan Baugh Save the Gators? Florida's offense has actually been impressive this season, averaging 41.7 points and 473.8 yards per game. Quarterback Aaron Philo has thrown for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions, while receiver Dallas Wilson has recorded 376 yards and three touchdowns. However, the biggest storyline is running back Jadan Baugh. Baugh has rushed for 672 yards and 12 touchdowns, establishing himself as one of the SEC's most productive backs. Unfortunately, his production has slowed considerably. Over Florida's last two games, Baugh has managed just 72 rushing yards, including 59 yards on 15 carries against South Carolina. That's a major concern considering Texas possesses one of the nation's best rushing defenses. Florida also defeated Texas 29-21 last season, meaning the Gators have already proven they're capable of beating Sarkisian's program. But winning in Austin will be a completely different challenge. How Each Team Wins For Texas, the formula starts with protecting Manning and establishing an early rhythm through the passing game. The Longhorns must take advantage of Florida's vulnerable secondary while allowing their defensive front to disrupt Philo and contain Baugh. For Florida, everything revolves around getting Baugh going early. If the Gators can establish their rushing attack, they'll have opportunities to control possession and keep Manning on the sidelines. Defensively, Florida must force Manning into mistakes, something Oklahoma successfully accomplished last weekend. I expect Texas to respond with a much more disciplined performance following its disappointing loss to Oklahoma. Manning should have opportunities to attack Florida's secondary, but I'm still not convinced he's capable of consistently dominating SEC competition. Expect a solid, rather than spectacular, performance from the Texas quarterback. The biggest difference will be Texas' defense. With Simmons creating pressure and the Longhorns limiting Baugh's rushing opportunities, Florida will struggle to sustain drives throughout the afternoon. I expect the Gators to keep things competitive early, but Texas will gradually take control in the second half. Final Score: No. 7 Texas 27, Florida 17 Texas gets back in the win column, improves to 5-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Florida Gators can put the Texas Longhorns' College Football Playoff hopes on life support this weekend in Austin. Both teams are looking to rebound from losses last weekend. Texas suffered its first loss of the season last Saturday, falling 27-24 to Oklahoma. Florida, meanwhile, has now lost two games after getting upset at home in a 38-19 loss to South Carolina. If Texas loses this weekend, they'll likely need to win out to make the 12-team playoff. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Florida vs Texas ESPN's Greg McElroy made his score predictions for this weekend's biggest games, and he has Texas beating Florida 31-17. "Where does Florida find 21 points?" said McElroy. "Florida scored 17 and 19 in their last two games against SEC defenses. When this (Texas) team allows fewer than 21 points, Steve Sarkisian is 63-4 as an FBS head coach. Now, Florida's best route there is the short field off of a Texas mistake because this Texas defense, they almost never let long drives finish in the end zone. "I'm taking Texas to win the game 31-17. I think Texas will win on third down all afternoon, because Florida's defense is probably going to have a hard time getting off the field, and I think Texas is built to live in short yardage. Florida's offense has stalled the last couple of weeks against SEC defenses, and this is the best defense I think they've seen so far. And that's no disrespect to South Carolina or Missouri — Texas is a step up in competition and personnel. … So we think Texas wins this game by a couple of touchdowns, but I do think both defenses will play well enough to keep it relatively low scoring. Texas wins this one slowly and on schedule. Whether or not we see the offensive fireworks is one of the biggest questions in the game." That may no longer be the case as junior quarterback Aaron Philo's “status is in question” entering Saturday's game against No. 7 Texas, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz . The Gators went 4-0 with Brown in the lineup this season, showcasing the nation's best offense to start the season. Brown is also a key part of Florida's special teams unit with two return touchdowns on the campaign. Florida QB Aaron Philo’s status in question vs. Texas; WR Vernell Brown III has ‘real shot’ to play | OnlyGators.com: Florida Gators news, analysis, schedules and scores OnlyGators.com: Florida Gators news, analysis, schedules and scores --> Home Image Credit:  Victoria Riccobono, UAA Philo's injury appears to be his shoulder. He was not mentioned as potentially missing the game by head coach Jon Sumrall in his weekly press conference on Monday, but given the reporting, it's likely that he has taken a back seat in practice this week. Offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner ran Philo 13 times in a loss to South Carolina. The SEC's availability report is initially released Wednesday night during the season. away.headline: Florida QB Aaron Philo's status is uncertain ahead of Texas game
away.blurb: According to Zenitz, Philo has "been limited" in practice this week as he deals with an injury. If he is unable to play, Zenitz believes backup Tramell Jones would get the start, the first of his career. Florida will release its first availability report ahead of the game on Wednesday night, which should provide more information on Philo's availability. The status of starting quarterback Aaron Philo is uncertain as the Florida Gators prepare for a massive showdown with the Texas Longhorns , according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. Philo, who competed with Jones for the starting job, has started all six of Florida's games this year, completing 105 of his 149 passes (70.4%) for 1,341 yards, nine touchdowns, and three interceptions. He has also run for 104 yards and three touchdowns on 44 carries. It is his first season as a starter after he spent the past two seasons as Georgia Tech's backup before following Buster Faulkner to Gainesville this offseason. He has thrown for 252 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions, completing 23 of his 29 attempts (79.3%). He has five carries for 25 yards. STARKVILLE — Mississippi State football fans have been asking the same big question ever since the lopsided loss to Alabama. Will star quarterback Kamario Taylor be healthy enough to play when the No. 19 Bulldogs (4-1, 2-1 SEC) face No. 21 LSU (4-2, 1-2) at Tiger Stadium on Oct. 17 (11 a.m., ESPN)? MSU coach Jeff Lebby has provided few details about Taylor's injury that forced him to watch the fourth quarter of the Alabama game from the sideline with a boot on his right foot. MSU has not said what his exact injury is. The first SEC availability report will release Oct. 14 with nightly updates until 90 minutes before kickoff. It's possible Taylor plays against LSU, but is it worth the risk? And, what if he doesn't play? Does Mississippi State stand a chance to beat LSU? Should Kamario Taylor play vs LSU if he's not healthy? The Bulldogs played Taylor when he wasn't at full speed vs Alabama, and it did not work well. Taylor, who entered that game among the favorites to win the Heisman Trophy, had his worst game of the season. It started with a lost fumble on the first drive and then a pick-six the next drive. "He is a problem in both areas when he's healthy of being able to run the ball. home.blurb: ESPN's Pete Thamel reported on Oct. 12 that Taylor has been a limited participant in practice. Taylor was limited mobility-wise with only one designed run in the game. This article originally appeared on Mississippi Clarion Ledger: Should Mississippi State risk playing QB Kamario Taylor vs LSU if he's limited? STARKVILLE — Mississippi State football fans have been asking the same big question ever since the lopsided loss to Alabama. Will star quarterback Kamario Taylor be healthy enough to play when the No. 19 Bulldogs (4-1, 2-1 SEC) face No. 21 LSU (4-2, 1-2) at Tiger Stadium on Oct. 17 (11 a.m., ESPN)? MSU coach Jeff Lebby has provided few details about Taylor's injury that forced him to watch the fourth quarter of the Alabama game from the sideline with a boot on his right foot. MSU has not said what his exact injury is. The first SEC availability report will release Oct. 14 with nightly updates until 90 minutes before kickoff. It's possible Taylor plays against LSU, but is it worth the risk? And, what if he doesn't play? Does Mississippi State stand a chance to beat LSU? Should Kamario Taylor play vs LSU if he's not healthy? The Bulldogs played Taylor when he wasn't at full speed vs Alabama, and it did not work well. Taylor, who entered that game among the favorites to win the Heisman Trophy, had his worst game of the season. It started with a lost fumble on the first drive and then a pick-six the next drive. The Bulldogs lost, 56-23, tying the largest loss under Jeff Lebby. "He's responded in a really good way," Lebby said of Taylor. MORE: How Kamario Taylor made ex-Mississippi State QB Omarr Conner such a proud uncle So, if Taylor isn't close to 100% healthy against LSU, is it worth him playing? That's something Lebby must decide when looking at the bigger picture of the season and weighing the risk of re-injury. Perhaps it'd be a different answer if Mississippi State had a worse record. The Bulldogs have no open weeks remaining and six of the seven remaining games are against SEC opponents. "He is really good," LSU coach Lane Kiffin said of Taylor. "He is a problem in both areas when he's healthy of being able to run the ball. We just played him last year at the last place we were at (Ole Miss), and he made some really good plays, especially late in the game when he starts running around. Obviously, he's much better in Year 2. Lebby does a great job with quarterbacks." Lebby mentioned Billy Puckett and AJ Swann as possibilities. Puckett and Swann have been listed as co-backups to Taylor on the weekly depth charts. They both profile differently, but Puckett is the only quarterback besides Taylor to play this season. Puckett is a sophomore from Jackson Prep. home.blurb: If Taylor cannot play, Mississippi State has two scholarship quarterbacks available: AJ Swann and Billy Puckett. If Taylor is available, Saturday’s game will feature two of the SEC’s top passing offenses. LSU averages 311 passing yards per game, just ahead of Mississippi State’s 309. LSU could catch a break this week as it prepares to host 16th-ranked Mississippi State. LSU coverage brought to you by Rouses Markets www.audacy.com ESPN’s Pete Thamel reports Bulldogs starting quarterback Kamario Taylor continues to be bothered by a foot injury suffered in the October 3 loss to Alabama. Taylor’s status for Saturday’s game against 22nd-ranked LSU remains uncertain. Mississippi State coach Jeff Lebby was asked Monday for an update on Taylor’s injury. His response: “Wednesday’s going to do all the talking.” Wednesday is when the SEC releases its first availability report for Saturday’s games. Taylor has been one of the most dynamic quarterbacks in college football this season. LSU coach Lane Kiffin called him a problem when asked about the Bulldogs’ quarterback Monday. Taylor has completed 66 percent of his passes for 1,450 yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions. But after suffering the injury against Alabama, Taylor was not the same. He finished the 56-23 loss 19-of-34 for 258 yards, three touchdowns and a season-high two interceptions. Swann previously played at LSU in 2024, appearing in two games as a backup to Garrett Nussmeier. Before transferring to LSU, Swann started 12 games over two seasons at Vanderbilt. picks.blurb: Auburn @ Georgia Preview And Prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers' Ohtani dilemma NFL hot seats Champions League updates Heisman Watch Auburn @ Georgia Preview And Prediction Oct 10, 2026; Tuscaloosa, Alabama, USA; Georgia Bulldogs quarterback Gunner Stockton (14) directs teammate running back Nick Peal (30) during the third quarter against the Alabama Crimson Tide at Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium. Mandatory Credit: David Leong-Imagn Images Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:33 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 1 Georgia hosts Auburn in the Deep South's Oldest Rivalry. After dominating Alabama physically, the Bulldogs could embarrass the Tigers. The Deep South's Oldest Rivalry returns to Athens this Saturday as No. 1 Georgia (6-0) welcomes Auburn (3-2) to Sanford Stadium for a 3:30 p.m. ET showdown on ESPN. And this matchup could get ugly quickly. Kirby Smart's Bulldogs are coming off an impressive 20-17 road victory over Alabama, while Auburn suffered a disappointing 24-14 loss at Tennessee. Georgia has also won nine consecutive meetings against Auburn, including last year's 20-10 victory in Jordan-Hare Stadium. Georgia: The Bulldogs Are Built DIFFERENT Georgia might have delivered its most impressive performance of the season against Alabama. Despite missing its top two running backs, Nate Frazier and Chauncey Bowens, the Bulldogs rushed for 206 yards against one of the SEC's most talented defenses. Dwight Phillips Jr. stepped up in a major way, while Bo Walker provided additional production in the backfield. Quarterback Gunner Stockton was outstanding, completing 18 of 22 passes for 249 yards while accounting for two touchdowns. Through six games, Stockton has thrown for 1,298 yards and 14 touchdowns, completing more than 76% of his passes. Defensively, Georgia held Alabama quarterback Keelon Russell to just 185 passing yards while recording four sacks. With Chris Cole, Raylen Wilson, KJ Bolden, and Ellis Robinson IV leading the defense, Georgia has the personnel to completely overwhelm Auburn's offense. Auburn: Can the Tigers Even Keep This Competitive? Auburn enters Saturday with serious questions surrounding its offense. Quarterback Byrum Brown has thrown for approximately 1,055 yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions. While he's dangerous with his legs, his decision-making has been inconsistent. Against Tennessee, Brown rushed for 107 yards but threw two interceptions in the 24-14 loss. Wide receiver Keshaun Singleton has emerged as a reliable target, recording 29 receptions for 322 yards. However, Auburn's biggest concern might be its inability to consistently stop the run. Tennessee rushed for 237 yards against the Tigers last weekend. That's a terrible sign considering Georgia just rushed for more than 200 yards against Alabama without its top two backs. If Auburn can't contain Georgia's rushing attack, this game could be over by halftime. How Each Team Wins For Georgia, the formula is simple: establish the running game, control the line of scrimmage, and force Brown to beat its defense through the air. Stockton should have plenty of opportunities to attack Auburn's secondary once the Tigers begin loading the box. Defensively, Georgia must contain Brown's mobility and force him into obvious passing situations. For Auburn, everything starts with avoiding turnovers and creating explosive plays. Brown must use his legs to extend drives, while the Tigers' defense needs to generate pressure on Stockton. Auburn cannot afford to fall behind early and become one-dimensional. I don't see this game being particularly competitive. Georgia is coming off an emotional victory over Alabama, but Kirby Smart has built a program that rarely overlooks inferior opponents, especially rivals. The Bulldogs should dominate the line of scrimmage, and I expect another massive rushing performance regardless of whether Frazier and Bowens return. Stockton should have an efficient afternoon, throwing multiple touchdowns while Georgia's defense forces Brown into at least two turnovers. Expect the Bulldogs to establish a commanding lead before halftime and eventually begin rotating younger players into the game. Final Score: No. 1 Georgia 41, Auburn 10 Georgia dominates its oldest rival, improves to 7-0, and continues looking like the team to beat in college football. picks.headline: Predictions, picks, odds for Auburn's Week 7 game at Georgia
picks.blurb: Auburn's date with Georgia will be its second of four games against a ranked team on its October schedule. The Tigers failed their first test by losing to No. 14 Tennessee in Week 5, 24-14. Auburn will also face No. 21 LSU and No. 10 Ole Miss before the calendar flips to November. Georgia handled its first true test last Saturday, defeating No. 6 Alabama on the road, 20-17. The Bulldogs outgained Alabama, 455-346, but struggled in the penalty department, committing seven for 57 yards. The win, in addition to Texas' loss to unranked Oklahoma, pushed Georgia to the No. 1 spot in both the US LBM Coaches Poll and the Associated Press poll ahead of Week 7. The Bulldogs are the nation's No. 1 team for several reasons, most of which can be found in stats. Georgia ranks No. 2 nationally in points per game (46.2), and is No. 1 in the SEC in points allowed (14.0), which ranks No. 11 nationally. Georgia also produces 474.8 yards per game while allowing opponents to gain 261.5 per game. Georgia is also great at protecting quarterback Gunner Stockton as they have allowed only six sacks through the midway point of the regular season. Auburn is in the lower-tier of most SEC stat categories, but is among the conference's best in interceptions. Auburn has hauled in six interceptions this season, which is tied with LSU and Missouri for the third-most in the SEC. away.headline: Auburn suspends All-American linebacker Xavier Atkins for Georgia game
away.blurb: “We’ll keep it in house. That’ll be the only piece of it that I will be addressing. He won’t be available for us this week for the game,” Golesh told On3's Justin Hokanson . He was named to the Preseason All-SEC Team before the season and has arguably been Auburn 's best player this season, recording 37 tackles, 7.5 tackles for loss, 3.0 sacks, one interception, and three quarterback hurries in five games. He has started four of their games, but did not against Southern Miss, with Hokanson reporting that was due to "internal discipline." Atkins was named a Second-Team All-American and First-Team All-SEC member last year after making 84 tackles, 17.0 tackles for loss, 9.0 sacks, one interception, and two forced fumbles. It was his first season at Auburn after he spent his freshman season with the LSU Tigers . Auburn is looking to beat Georgia in Athens for the first time since 2005 this weekend, and will now be doing so without one of its best players. The Tigers opened as nearly three-touchdown underdogs against the Bulldogs. away.headline: Auburn’s Xavier Atkins Suspended From Team, Alex Golesh Says
away.blurb: “We will be without Xavier Atkins this week,” Golesh said. “We'll revisit it next week when we meet again on Monday in here. Keep it in-house in terms of anything beyond that. Really, that would be the only piece of it that I'll be addressing. He won't be with us this week for the game on Saturday, and he won’t be available. We’ll revisit early next week when we meet again here.” Atkins, who was a Second-Team All-American last season , will be a notable absence for the Tigers as they take on the No. 1 team in the country this weekend, though the Tigers will have plenty of other linebacker options available. Auburn’s Xavier Atkins Suspended From Team, Alex Golesh Says Skip to main content SI.COM The Auburn Tigers will head to Athens this weekend without the help of one of their top linebackers, as after much speculation this weekend, Alex Golesh announced on Monday that junior linebacker Xavier Atkins would not be participating in the Tigers’ upcoming matchup with the Georgia Bulldogs. It will be interesting to see how this decision affects the Tigers’ defense, as well as Atkins’ draft stock, since he was expected to be an early-round draft pick at the end of this season. Ideally, this suspension would last just one game, and Atkins would be ready for the LSU game next week. Leading off that group is Elijah Melendez, a sophomore in the midst of a breakout year. Melendez currently leads the Tigers in total tackles with 43, solo tackles with 28, pass deflections with four and ties Atkins for the lead in sacks with 3.0. However, after the duo of Melendez and Atkins, there is a pretty sharp drop-off on the stat sheet among the Tigers’ linebackers. Bryce Deas, another sophomore, ranks third on the list, though he’s only accumulated 15 total tackles and eight solo tackles this season. Then, De’Marcus Riddick, who was a Freshman All-SEC teamer in 2024, ranks fourth among linebackers with five total tackles, four of which were solo tackles. Likely, one or both of Deas or Riddick will need to step up for this matchup if the Tigers want to keep the Dawgs’ strong offense contained, especially without a premier defender like Atkins. Alex Golesh made it clear that he was not going to shy away from building a strong culture on the Plains in his first year, and he seems to be making the point that no player, regardless of skill, NIL, or accolades, is above reproach in his program. Whatever the reason, it certainly takes guts to bench a player like Atkins– we’ll see how it pays off. Loading recommendations... home.headline: Georgia Reveals Surprising Injury on Initial Report Which Could Have Huge Impact
home.blurb: While much of the focus has been on the weather, Wednesday evening revealed the initial injury availability report , and there was a significant Georgia player listed as out who nobody saw coming. Junior running back Chauncey Bowens, who was played an important role the last two seasons, is going to be out. The reports surrounding Bowens seem to indicate he was rolled up on during the win over Vanderbilt, with Dawgs Central even reporting that Bowens is in a walking boot this week. While the good news is that Nate Frazier is not on the report, one has to wonder just how healthy he is, and with Bowens now out, the Bulldogs all of the sudden look very thin at running back. Dwight Phillips Jr. -- who Kirby Smart has been heaping praise on the last couple of weeks -- will also undoubtedly be a key piece of the plan as well. Georgia has solid depth at the position, but Bowens being out along with Frazier likely being limited is a bit of a blow to the chances of winning the game. Bowens has been a key piece of the goal line attack with six rushing touchdowns on the year, and with 10 carries last week against Vanderbilt he led the attack. It was sophomore Bo Walker who made the most of his opportunities though with 71 yards on just five touches, and he is going to be a key piece this week as well. With weather conditions potentially brutal, establishing the run will be key, and an Alabama run defense that looks greatly improved this year certainly will love any edge they can get. More pressure is put on Gunner Stockton as well, but that's nothing he cannot handle. Injuries are a reality in this sport, and ultimately who manages them better can decide who is still standing at the end of a season. It's just another challenge for the Dawgs on a night that will be full of them, and Kirby Smart is being faced with one of the biggest regular season games of his career at Georgia. Time will tell how he and his team handle it.

Photo By - Reuters Connect. Alabama fans light up victory cigars to celebrate beating Tennessee. One of the SEC's best rivalry games returns for the 109th time since 1901, with Alabama and Tennessee playing at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville, Tenn., on Saturday at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC). A game known as the "Third Saturday in October" for when it's historically been played, the Crimson Tide had been dominating the Alabama vs. Tennessee rivalry during the Nick Saban era, but the programs have split the series over the last four years. Despite the Volunteers catching up to the Crimson Tide in recent seasons, Alabama is a 9.5-point favorite and the popular pick among college football analysts . Alabama vs Tennessee rivalry history: Third Saturday in October 60 (1 win vacated) 40 (1 win vacated) 15 (2007-2021) Longest win streak 7 (1995-2001) Largest margin of victory 992-346-43 (.734) Program record 892-424-55 (.671) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks Alabama and Tennessee's rivalry has long been filled with winning streaks, legendary coaches, and cigars. The Crimson Tide and Volunteers played for the first time in 1901, with the programs tying 6-6 in Birmingham, Ala., the home of the rivalry for seven of the first eight meetings. However, the game wasn't initially played on the third Saturday in October (it was played in November), nor every season. For the first 26 years of the rivalry, Alabama and Tennessee played just 11 times, which included the teams not playing at all between 1915 and 1927. Over those first 11 meetings, Alabama went 8-2-1 and didn't allow a Tennessee touchdown from 1903 to 1913. The rivalry returned in full in October 1928, and Alabama and Tennessee have only gone without playing for one season since then, and that was in 1943 due to World War II. The return of the rivalry also coincided with Tennessee becoming a powerhouse under Robert Neyland, who was hired in 1926. That helped Tennessee turn it into a competitive rivalry, with the Volunteers going 20-15-6 from the 1920s through the 1960s. But that's when Alabama changed college football forever after hiring Texas A&M's coach, who had earned his nickname after agreeing to wrestle a bear when he was 13 years old. Paul "Bear" Bryant would beat Tennessee for the first time in 1961 and win on the third Saturday in October 16 times from '61 to '81, taking home six national championships in the process. The rivalry would resume its competitiveness in the 1980s thanks to Johnny Majors, with Tennessee owning Alabama in the 1990s under Phillip Fulmer. But then everything changed when Alabama brought the only college football coach better than Bryant to Tuscaloosa in 2007. Saban went 16-1 against Tennessee. But with Saban gone, the rivalry has been split the last two years under Kalen DeBoer. The first game between Alabama and Tennessee was on Nov. 28, 1901, in Birmingham, Ala. The two programs tied 6-6, the only time both teams scored points in the first 10 meetings. In 1901, Tennessee was held scoreless when Alabama won 24-0, and then the Volunteers shut out the Crimson Tide 5-0 in 1904. From 1905 to 1913, Alabama won seven straight against Tennessee, outscoring the Vols 112-0 (Tennessee would win 17-7 in 1914). After more than a decade-long hiatus, the rivalry returned in 1928 and became one of the top SEC rivalries thanks to Neyland. Why does the winner of Alabama vs. Tennessee smoke victory cigars? One of the most unique aspects of Alabama and Tennessee's rivalry is the victory cigars. The winning team lights up a victory cigar in its locker room following the game, and fans light them up in the stands of the stadium to celebrate a win. The tradition began in the 1950s when Alabama's athletic trainer Jim Goostree began handing out cigars following a win over Tennessee. Both programs continued the tradition, which began as a secret due to NCAA rules around extra benefits for players and use of tobacco products. In 2005, Alabama publicly brought the tradition back to the forefront of the rivalry but had to self-report it as an NCAA violation as a result. However, since 2007, the winner of Alabama vs. Tennessee has knowingly and openly violated the NCAA rule and reported said violation to the NCAA as part of the tradition. Why is it called the Third Saturday in October? This name is pretty self-explanatory, with Alabama vs. Tennessee being played on the third Saturday in October every season. The tradition began when Neyland started consistently scheduling the matchup against the Crimson Tide on the third Saturday in October, with the rivalry officially adopting the name of "Third Saturday in October" in 1939. Though the game hasn't actually always fallen on the third Saturday in October over the decades due to SEC scheduling and conference changes, the rivalry name of the "Third Saturday in October" has remained. Best moments in the Alabama vs Tennessee rivalry The Bear's streak ends (1982) Before Saban, there was Bryant, and the Bear didn't often lose on the third Saturday in October. When he initially took over Alabama in 1958, Bryant got off to a rough start against Tennessee, going 0-2-1. But between 1961 and 1981, Bryant was 16-4-1 against Tennessee, including an 11-game winning streak from 1971 to 1981. In 1982, Tennessee shocked the college football world after ending the streak. The Volunteers' legendary head coach Johnny Majors led his team to a 35-28 upset of No. 2 Alabama. Bryant would return for just one more season in Tuscaloosa, with Majors once again getting the best of the Bear, and Tennessee beating No. 11 Alabama 41-34. The five-overtime game (2003) Tennessee was looking to bounce back from a loss to Alabama in 2002, its first since 1994, in a clash that resulted in the longest game in the history of the rivalry. The No. 22 Volunteers came back from down 20-13 in the fourth quarter when Casey Clausen led a game-tying drive with 30 seconds left to force overtime. Tennessee managed to convert a 4th-and-19 to stay alive during double OT, and in the fifth OT, Clausen scored to pull off a 51-43 win in Tuscaloosa. The game lasted four hours and 53 minutes. The goalposts go for a swim when the drought ends (2022) One of the most improbable wins in the history of the Alabama-Tennessee rivalry came in 2022, when Saban was riding a 15-game winning streak (the longest in the rivalry's history) into Knoxville. Saban had owned the Vols for a decade and a half, recording double-digit wins in 13 of the 15 straight victories and handing Tennessee four of the largest blowout defeats in rivalry history. Landon Kardian Tue, October 13, 2026 at 8:42 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads No. 6 Alabama travels to No. 14 Tennessee for a massive SEC rivalry showdown. Can Keelon Russell bounce back and keep the Tide's playoff hopes alive? One of college football's greatest rivalries returns Saturday afternoon as No. 6 Alabama (5-1) travels to Knoxville to face No. 14 Tennessee (5-1) in the Third Saturday in October showdown. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET on ABC, and both programs have plenty to prove. Alabama is coming off a heartbreaking 20-17 loss to Georgia, while Tennessee narrowly escaped Arkansas with a 24-17 victory. The Crimson Tide defeated Tennessee 37-20 last season, but the Volunteers have won the last two meetings in Knoxville. With both teams fighting for College Football Playoff positioning, Saturday's matchup could have enormous consequences. Alabama: Can Keelon Russell Bounce Back? Alabama's offense has been one of the nation's most explosive units, averaging 44.2 points per game. Quarterback Keelon Russell has thrown for 1,599 yards, 12 touchdowns, and just two interceptions while adding 225 rushing yards and four scores. However, Georgia exposed some weaknesses in the sophomore quarterback's game. Russell completed just 16 of 30 passes for 185 yards and one touchdown against the Bulldogs, struggling to consistently move the football against an elite defense. Saturday presents another difficult challenge. Tennessee is allowing just 15.5 points per game and has surrendered only three passing touchdowns through six games. Making matters worse, Alabama is expected to be without leading receiver Ryan Coleman-Williams, who has recorded 415 receiving yards and four touchdowns. That means Lotzeir Brooks, who has 389 receiving yards, and Rico Scott will need to step up. The Crimson Tide must also establish their rushing attack to prevent Tennessee from putting all its attention on Russell. Tennessee: The Volunteers Have a MAJOR Problem Tennessee has managed to win five of its first six games, but Josh Heupel's offense has serious questions at quarterback. Freshman Faizon Brandon has battled a shoulder injury, forcing George MacIntyre into his first career start against Arkansas. MacIntyre completed 18 of 29 passes for 247 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions. And against Alabama's talented secondary, those mistakes could prove extremely costly. The Volunteers rank just 110th nationally in passing offense, averaging 186.5 yards per game. However, Tennessee has been outstanding on the ground. Running back DeSean Bishop has rushed for 678 yards and eight touchdowns, helping Tennessee average 228.3 rushing yards per game. Bishop will be the biggest threat to Alabama's defense, especially considering Georgia rushed for more than 200 yards against the Crimson Tide last weekend. Wide receiver Mike Matthews, who leads Tennessee with 396 receiving yards, could also create problems if Alabama becomes too focused on stopping the run. How Each Team Wins For Alabama, the formula starts with forcing Tennessee to throw the football. If the Crimson Tide can contain Bishop and put the Volunteers into third-and-long situations, their defense should have opportunities to create turnovers. Offensively, Russell must protect the football, utilize his mobility, and attack Tennessee's secondary without forcing unnecessary throws. For Tennessee, everything revolves around establishing the rushing attack and controlling possession. The Volunteers must also generate consistent pressure on Russell and prevent Alabama from creating explosive plays downfield. A loud Neyland Stadium crowd could make things difficult for Alabama, particularly if Tennessee establishes an early lead. I expect a physical, defensive battle between two SEC rivals. Tennessee's rushing attack will create problems early, but I don't trust the Volunteers' quarterback situation against Alabama's defense. Whether it's Brandon or MacIntyre under center, Tennessee simply hasn't demonstrated enough consistency throwing the football. Russell should respond with a much cleaner performance after struggling against Georgia, although I don't expect Alabama's offense to put up its usual explosive numbers. The Crimson Tide will establish a narrow lead before halftime and gradually take control in the second half. I expect Alabama's defense to force multiple turnovers, while Russell makes enough plays to secure a comfortable road victory. Final Score: No. 6 Alabama 24, No. 14 Tennessee 13 Alabama gets back on track, improves to 6-1, and keeps its College Football Playoff hopes alive. picks.blurb: Alabama Football 2026: Previewing the Tennessee Offense - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers' Ohtani dilemma NFL hot seats Champions League updates Heisman Watch Alabama Football 2026: Previewing the Tennessee Offense FAYETTEVILLE, ARKANSAS - OCTOBER 10: DeSean Bishop #18 of the Tennessee Volunteers runs the ball in the first half during the game against the Arkansas Razorbacks at Donald W. Reynolds Razorback Stadium on October 10, 2026 in Fayetteville, Arkansas. (Photo by Wesley Hitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brent Taylor Wed, October 14, 2026 at 12:56 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As much as things keep changing in college football, the one constant for me the last few years has been my previews for the Tennessee offense each season. Josh Heupel is now in year 6 in Knoxville, and OC Joey Halzle has been calling the plays since Alex Golesh left for USF back in 2023. The Heupel offense is one that's famously predicated on putting wide receivers WAAAY wide to force the defense into spread out formations, then attacking downfield with switch release routes or quick screens. And they operate as fast as possible, trying to trap defenses into personnel with warp speed snapping and doing more post-snap reads. Where the Vols offense has evolved over the years, though, is how much they've made the run game the central aspect of their attack, rather than the passing game. Sure, they're spread out wide and going fast, but they make a LOT of hay with just straight inside zone runs. They're averaging a respectable 34.7 points per game, but the caveat is that they scored most of their points on Furman, Georgia Tech, and Kennesaw State, and since moving to SEC play they've scored 17 vs Texas, 24 against Auburn, and 24 against the corpse of Arkansas. Through it, the Vols have been one of the best rushing teams in the country. They're putting up 228 yards per game, with star running back DeSean Bishop already at 678 yards and 8 touchdowns on an impressive 6.3 yards per carry through 6 games. In particular, Bishop put up 258 of his yards this season the last two weeks. And he was also a 1000 yard rusher for the Vols a year ago, and put up 123 yards against Alabama in 2025. He's one of the best backs in college football. He's impressively tough to tackle, plays with a lot of power, and, most importantly, is a maestro at hitting cutbacks in their zone blocking scheme. While the Vols' rushing attack has been stellar, the passing game is where they've struggled. They're only averaging 187 yards per game. QB Faizon Brandon is a 5-star true freshman who was the #10 overall recruit in the last recruiting cycle, and while he brought a lot of excitement to the Vol fanbase, he's generally showed his age and inexperience through the first part of the season, struggling with taking sacks and running himself into pressure. Brandon picked up a shoulder injury at some point, and sophomore George MacIntyre took over for the Arkansas game last week in a sort-of-injury, sort-of-benching situation for Brandon. MacIntyre did pass for over 200 yards, but he still took two sacks and threw two picks, so there wasn't a whole lot of improvement. To this point, Brandon is back practicing for the Vols this week, but we don't actually know who will wind up being the guy against Alabama. At wide receiver, the limited passing game has almost solely gone through returning starters Braylon Staley and Mike Matthews. Staley is something of an old-school possession receiver who excels at moving the chains. He leads the team with 24 catches, but only has 193 total yards with that. His running mate, Mike Matthews, is the downfield threat, turning 22 catches into 396 yards. There's a smattering of other receivers and tight ends with a few catches, but for the most part, the ball is either going to Staley or Matthews. As far as the offensive line… It's been downright offensive. The worst was when they played Texas and gave up 10 sacks in one day. They been generally solid at run blocking (except against Texas), but the pass blocking has left a lot to be desired. This will be the third year in a row that the Huepel/Halzle takes on the Kane Wommack defense. In both years, the Vols scored 24 and 20 points, despite coming into the game scoring a whole lot more points. Wommack's simple zone coverage focus has seemed to help them with Huepel's outside stacks and releases, making this scheme match up much better than Saban's pattern match in 2022. Still, the Alabama defense has been reeling recently, giving up a lot of inside rushing yards to UGA and struggling to break up downfield deep shots all season. I think that Bishop will get over 100 yards on the Tide, unfortunately. However, I also don't think that UT has the QB play to really be able to move the chains constantly on the Tide, ultimately limiting them to about 17 points, with a strong contingent of turnovers/sacks ending drives.

away.blurb: Eleven of the 16 players who were on Missouri football's pregame availability reports between Wednesday and Friday were removed from the final pregame report, meaning all players who were not previously ruled out are available to play against Texas A&M. Mizzou had 16 players listed with five players listed as “out,” seven players listed as “questionable” and four players listed as “probable.” Now, the Tigers only have five players on the report, each of whom were already ruled out of playing against the Aggies. That means all of the following players should be able to play against Texas A&M: starting left tackle Cayden Green, starting defensive ends Langden Kitchen and Darris Smith, starting linebacker Robert Woodyard Jr., starting safeties Santana Banner and Kensley Louidor-Faustin, return specialist/wide receiver DaMarion Fowlkes, starting tight end Brett Norfleet, rotational cornerback Jahlil Florence, rotational defensive end Jaden Jones and backup linebacker Bobby Washington. The five players who were ruled out are running backs Ahmad Hardy and Malae Fonoti, backup safety JaDon Blair, reserve tight end Gavin Hoffman and right tackle Josh Atkins. The possible designations, from most likely to play to least likely, are as follows: available; probable; questionable/game-time decision; doubtful; out. Texas A&M (3-2, 1-2) listed three players on its final report. Most notably, starting wide receiver Mario Craver is listed as a "game-time decision." Offensive lineman Blake Ivy and wideout Terry Bussey have been ruled out. This article originally appeared on Columbia Daily Tribune: Missouri football injury report Texas A&M: Tigers make 11 players available The SEC-mandated reports are required of member organizations every night beginning Wednesday in the leadup to an in-conference matchup, with the final report publishing 90 minutes before kickoff. away.headline: Missouri's extensive injury report is looking increasingly like a nothingburger
away.blurb: The injury reports for Texas A&M and Missouri could not have looked more different coming into their huge game this morning, but it's looking more and more like that was all for show. The Aggies were down Terry Bussey (who is out for the season) and Blake Ivy, with Mario Craver listed as questionable, but it was the laundry list of players on Missouri's side that caught the eye of fans. The Tigers had listed as questionable players like star OL Cayden Green, starting S Santana Banner, and star Auburn transfer LB Robert Woodyard— in all, three of their top four tacklers on defense, as well as a remarkable number of offensive weapons. However, as game time has drawn nearer this morning, it looks like all of the hubbub around Missouri's potential missing players is possibly for naught. Reporting is emerging that some of the big time players for the Tigers that were listed as questionable in this game are on track to play, showing that the Aggies will indeed be facing a Mizzou team at nearly-full strength this week. Pete Thamel of ESPN reports that the Tigers' starting edge defenders, Darris Smith and Langden Kitchen, will both be playing against A&M in this game as well; both had been listed as questionable coming into the game. The game day update of the injury report confirms this from Thamel and Zenitz, as every single player that was listed as questionable or probable for the Tigers has been removed from the list , apparently set to play in this one. That's not only dismaying for the Aggies, it's a bit questionable on the part of the Tigers. We saw some interesting usage of the report by Lane Kiffin earlier this season, and though Eli Drinkwitz likes to do a bit of trolling from time to time, he doesn't quite have the same reputation as the LSU head coach does. While that's not an accusation that he was definitively misusing the report, it is odd that not a single player of the seven listed on the report as questionable actually will end up being unavailable for this game. That said, though, just because a player is not listed as "out" on this report does not mean that they are a sure thing to play in the game: we saw that with Jamarion Morrow last week for the Aggies. Texas A&M's optimism suddenly tamped down as Missouri's injury report apparently set to shrink Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reports that Green, Banner, and Woodyard are all set to play in this game, which will be a huge relief for Tiger fans— but grim news for the Aggies, who definitely need all the help they can get in this one. In all, though, this means that Texas A&M will indeed have a challenge ahead of them today of a Tigers team at almost full strength. The Aggies need this win, but it was never going to come easy— this development only underlines that fact. away.headline: Ex-Rebels lead No. 13 Missouri into Oxford to face No. 9 Ole Miss
away.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren't made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it's worth noting that Simmons' Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. "I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder," tailback Jamal Roberts said. "We definitely can let them guys handle that." No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. "The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is," Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. "There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides." "We talk about the joy of the journey," Drinkwitz said. "That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don't think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that." Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers' biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He's completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. "He's playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they're already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou's top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. "He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape," Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. "They're a total team," Drinkwitz said. "We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game." In Mizzou's most recent road game, the Tigers blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost at Mississippi State. Drinkwitz said they had better learn from the experience. home.blurb: Simmons, top receiver Cayden Lee and cornerback Chris Graves Jr. weren't made available to speak Tuesday about transferring from Ole Miss, but it's worth noting that Simmons' Instagram account still has a number of posts from his years in Oxford. "I feel like those guys are definitely going to come out and play with a chip on their shoulder," tailback Jamal Roberts said. "We definitely can let them guys handle that." No. 9 Ole Miss reached the College Football Playoff semifinals a season ago with Trinidad Chambliss at quarterback after Simmons went down early with an injury and lost his starting job. Tigers coach Eli Drinkwitz acknowledged that the game will be a big deal for Simmons, along with two other Mizzou players imported from Ole Miss. Drinkwitz just wants them to keep perspective, considering about 20% of FBS players are transfers. "The biggest thing is to not make it bigger than it is," Drinkwitz told reporters Tuesday. "There are great memories from there. I think everybody left there in a positive light on both sides." "We talk about the joy of the journey," Drinkwitz said. "That was a part of their journey that made them who they are right now. I don't think there has to be a whole lot more to it than that." Mizzou (5-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) comes in having won two straight home games against SEC foes, most recently 27-6 over Texas A&M on Saturday. The Tigers' biggest win so far came against Florida, 45-17 on Oct. 3. Simmons has been terrific for the Tigers, ranking 11th in FBS in passing efficiency rating. He's completing 65% of his passes, with 14 touchdowns and one interception in 165 attempts. "He's playing as an experienced quarterback in a really good system," Ole Miss coach Pete Golding said. Lee has scored five touchdowns while leading the Tigers with 42 receptions and 616 yards. He and Simmons may be transfers, but they're already leaders at Mizzou, other players say. Roberts will be another focal point for Ole Miss. After putting together two straight games of 200-plus yards, he ranks first in the SEC and second nationally with 828 rushing yards. Mizzou's top back a season ago, Ahmad Hardy, is recovering from an offseason gunshot wound. Golding said that Ole Miss (4-1, 2-1 SEC) will have its hands full trying to tackle Roberts. "He has the most yards after contact right now, which is something that has been an issue for us on tape," Golding said. With Chambliss continuing to rank as a Heisman Trophy contender and NFL prospect, Ole Miss routed Vanderbilt 52-17 on Saturday. The Rebels also have wins against ranked opponents LSU and Louisville. "They're a total team," Drinkwitz said. "We need to play our best, most complete game to even be in the game." In Mizzou's most recent road game, the Tigers blew a fourth-quarter lead and lost at Mississippi State. Drinkwitz said they had better learn from the experience.
