Can the struggling Seminoles avoid another embarrassing defeat? One of college football's fiercest rivalries returns as No. 3 Miami (5-0) hosts Florida State (3-3) at Hard Rock Stadium. These two programs couldn't be heading in more different directions. Miami is coming off a dominant 41-13 victory over Clemson and remains firmly in the national championship conversation. Meanwhile, Florida State suffered an embarrassing 44-20 loss to Louisville after blowing an early 14-0 lead. With Miami entering as a heavy favorite, Mike Norvell and the Seminoles could be in serious trouble. Miami: The Hurricanes Look UNSTOPPABLE Mario Cristobal has built one of the most complete teams in college football, and quarterback Darian Mensah is playing like a legitimate Heisman Trophy contender. Mensah has thrown for 1,438 yards, 15 touchdowns, and zero interceptions this season. Miami is averaging an incredible 49.6 points per game while allowing just 9.8. Freshman sensation Malachi Toney has been nearly impossible to defend, recording 604 receiving yards and six touchdowns. His explosiveness gives Miami a dangerous weapon against a Florida State secondary that has struggled against quality competition. Running back Mark Fletcher Jr. provides another dimension to the offense, and Miami should have opportunities to establish the run against a vulnerable Seminoles defense. Florida State: Mike Norvell Is Running Out of Answers Florida State's season has quickly become a disappointment. The Seminoles allowed an unbelievable 397 rushing yards against Louisville, including 235 yards from Isaac Brown. That's a massive problem against Miami's balanced offense. Quarterback Ashton Daniels has thrown for 1,320 yards, eight touchdowns, and seven interceptions this season. Although Daniels has been dangerous with his legs, his inconsistency as a passer could become a serious issue against Miami's defense. Running back Ousmane Kromah has been productive with 565 rushing yards, but the Seminoles cannot rely entirely on their ground game if Miami builds an early lead. Florida State has enough athleticism to make some plays, but its defensive struggles and offensive turnovers make this an extremely difficult matchup. How Each Team Wins For Miami, the formula is simple: establish the run, protect the football, and allow Mensah to attack Florida State's secondary. Defensively, the Hurricanes must contain Daniels' rushing ability and force him to win from the pocket. For Florida State, everything starts with controlling possession. The Seminoles must establish Kromah, limit Miami's explosive plays, and create turnovers. If Florida State allows this game to become a shootout, it could get ugly quickly. I simply don't see Florida State having enough answers for Miami's offense. Mensah has been outstanding, and I expect him to continue his Heisman-caliber season against a Seminoles defense that just surrendered 44 points to Louisville. Florida State should create a few explosive plays with Daniels and Kromah, especially early, but Miami's defense will eventually take control. I expect the Hurricanes to establish a comfortable halftime lead before completely taking over in the second half. Final Score: No. 3 Miami 45, Florida State 20 Miami remains undefeated, improves to 6-0, and strengthens its national championship case. away.blurb: After pulling off a win over Virginia in Week 5 with plenty of injuries , Florida State will need to do it all over again with Louisville looming this weekend. The first Week 6 injury report has already been made available, and even at full strength, the Seminoles will be entering the game with a number of players banged up. Playing through injuries and adapting quickly can be tough, but Louisville will have to do the same thing, and Florida State needs to take advantage. The Cardinals have a handful of players who have already been ruled out for the game, and that part of the injury report has mainly stayed the same over the past few weeks. There are a few new additions to the report that could be important, including starting offensive lineman Cason Henry. Henry, who is listed as questionable for the game, is a starting tackle for Louisville who has been a key part of the run game for the Cardinals. Florida State improved as a unit defensively against Virginia, but the team still struggles in a few areas. The Seminoles allow 119.2 rushing yards per game, and even with a talented passing attack, the Cardinals are going to try to establish the run. Louisville might be entering the game without two starters on the offensive line, but another injury situation to monitor involves running back Keyjuan Brown. Last week, during the loss to NC State, Brown carried the football just eight times and fumbled twice, losing both fumbles. Brown is now listed as questionable for the upcoming game, and losing the leading rusher for the Florida State game would be a tough blow. The injuries have been piling on this season for Florida State, from starters to backups, and even a few reserve players. The team has never truly played at 100% this season, but that has not stopped the Seminoles from finding success. Each team deals with injuries, however, and it is the job of the opponent to find a way to use those situations to their advantage. home.headline: As players return, Miami Hurricanes’ defensive versatility will be on full display
home.blurb: Nevertheless, seeing it play out as it did in a live game setting was encouraging for Miami as it sorted through its options as key players were sidelined — and was only one such example over the past month. The Hurricanes (5-0, 3-0 Atlantic Coast Conference) have played the past four weeks without starting cornerbacks OJ Frederique Jr. and Xavier Lucas, both of whom were hurt in the season opener against Stanford. A third cornerback expected to contribute in Ja’Boree Antoine hasn’t played yet this season. A fourth in Damari Brown has been limited. Added Cristobal: “The versatility that we were able to work with in practice and then actually use in the game has helped out a lot. Those guys are really highly intelligent, with real high normal IQs and football IQs. We have mixed and matched those guys every which way you can imagine. So that comes into play now and allows for competition to get ramped up.” It has worked out for Miami, with the Hurricanes leading the country in scoring defense (9.8 points allowed per game) and ranking sixth in total yards allowed per game (249.6). “I tell guys this ‘young guy’ stuff, throw that out the window,” Cristobal said. “You’re compensated. You’ve been here since January. Throw that out the window. Have maturity. Approach everything like a professional, and I think that approach has helped us develop a little bit faster, has accelerated some of that, so we’ll see what it looks like on game day.” The sophomore excelled in the new role, which didn’t surprise his coaches considering Fitzgerald’s ball-hawking nature and strong defensive instincts. Now, as the Hurricanes’ defense gets closer to full strength as it prepares for a home game against in-state rival Florida State on Saturday (7 p.m., ESPN), that positional versatility could be a boon for Miami moving forward. “We’ve been cross-training throughout the summer and throughout the spring,” safety Zechariah Poyser said, “but there’s nothing like game reps. So seeing everybody get those game reps and keep getting experience, it’s definitely amazing for the long run.” And was needed in the short run. Lucas and Brown are “all the way back” this week, according to coach Mario Cristobal, but those absences led to the Hurricanes using a lot of moving parts on the back end of the defense. Fitzgerald, who had a team-high six interceptions last season primarily playing safety and nickel, added outside corner to his repertoire. picks.headline: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling
picks.blurb: Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Dodgers' Ohtani dilemma NFL hot seats Champions League updates Heisman Watch Story by Wildcats Wire Oklahoma offense preview: Can Kentucky keep the Sooners struggling Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 4:11 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football travels down to Norman to face the Oklahoma Sooners on Saturday, and both of these teams have plenty of momentum coming into this matchup. Arguably no team in the country has more momentum on their side than the Wildcats right now, coming off back-to-back walk off two-point conversions for the win in overtime. However, Oklahoma came off of their bye week and got a massive win over Texas in the Red River Rivalry game. With that being said, do not let the final score fool you, Oklahoma is still really struggling on offense. Oklahoma's offense will be the worst unit on the field this Saturday, and despite a big 27-24 win over Texas, the issues have not been fixed. The Sooners have scored just six offensive touchdowns since week two. They have only scored over 20 points twice this season, this was week one against UTEP and against Texas where they needed a blocked punt for a touchdown and a pick six to do so. This is a night game in Norman and will present a lot of adversity for Kentucky. The matchup to watch is the Kentucky offense versus the Oklahoma defense, but we will get into that side later. Basically every single offensive metric that you look at to determine offensive success, the Sooners rank bottom five in the SEC. Oklahoma ranks dead last in the conference in all of these statistics: Success rate, Rush SR%, EPA per rush, Explosive play rate and 1D+TD%. They also rank bottom five in the SEC in these statistics: EPA per play, EPA per dropback, Pass SR%, 3rd Down conversion rate, Early Down conversion rate and yards per play. This might be the worst offense Kentucky faces this season unless they can turn things around quickly. Oklahoma ranks first in the SEC in three-and-out rate and negative play percentage. The Sooners have the worst yards per carry average in the FBS. This is a stark contrast because Kentucky's defense ranks top five in the SEC in explosive % allowed and negative % forced. Kentucky's defense has excelled at three things this season: forcing turnovers, forcing negative plays and limiting explosives. This Oklahoma offense has struggled, but they do have some playmakers. The number one guy that should scare you, ironically, is number one Isaiah Sategna. Sategna is a dynamic receiver who is the one guy that can consistently create separation and he is dangerous with the football in his hands. Kentucky has to know where Sategna is on every snap because he is lightning in a bottle when he gets his hands on the football. John Mateer is a reckless but talented quarterback, he made the best throw of his season against Texas to set up the Sooners for the game winning field goal. Mateer threw a perfect back shoulder to Sategna from the far hash. Mateer has arm talent and is a dangerous runner, he immediately looks to run when a pass play breaks down. However, Mateer is extremely turnover prone, even moreso than LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt. Kentucky forced two turnovers on Leavitt, and they need to repeat that on Saturday. They have done a great job of forcing turnovers all season, they did it against Keelon Russell, Marcel Reed, LaNorris Sellers and Leavitt. This defensive line has to get pressure on Mateer to force him to play recklessly. The Wildcats have struggled with scrambling quarterbacks this season, but they were better last week against Leavitt--same thing applies this week with Mateer. Oklahoma as we stated, averages the fewest yards per carry in all of FBS. This is a game where Kentucky should be able to make Oklahoma one dimensional, which is a massive advantage for the Wildcats. The defense has to make Mateer uncomfortable in the pocket and they will have a great chance to win this football game. Kentucky's defense has the opportunity to have their best performance of the season this Saturday. What a wild Saturday it was for the Kentucky Football team. The Wildcats escaped with a 35-34 overtime victory over then-No. 10 LSU Tigers inside Kroger Field while rocking the iconic Power K jerseys. The game featured plenty of twists and turns, including trick plays that resulted in LSU touchdowns, explosive plays from Kentucky’s offense and special teams, turnovers, and, most importantly, missed field goals. Through it all, Kentucky remained competitive. With LSU facing a fourth-down situation late in regulation, the Tigers elected to punt rather than go for it. Kentucky then drove down the field in less than two minutes, setting up kicker Adam Zouagui for a field goal to send the game into overtime after he had missed his previous two attempts. Kentucky won the coin toss and elected to play defense first. LSU quickly drove down the field and scored a touchdown. The Wildcats then got their opportunity, and on third-and-10, quarterback Kenny Minchey connected with Kenny Darby, who nearly took the ball into the end zone but came up a yard short. CJ Baxter immediately punched it in for a touchdown, leaving Kentucky down by one point. Instead of kicking the extra point to force a second overtime, first-year head coach Will Stein decided to go for the two-point conversion to win the game. The decision paid off. Minchey called his own number on a quarterback draw, found plenty of open space, and crossed the goal line untouched to secure the victory. Kentucky defeated LSU 35-34 in overtime, improving to 5-1 overall and 3-1 in SEC play. The Wildcats are now ranked No. 15 in the AP Top 25 poll. Oklahoma Sooners (3-2, 1-1 in SEC) The Oklahoma Sooners have faced increased scrutiny this season after finishing the 2025 campaign with a 10-3 record and earning a spot in the College Football Playoff. However, their season ended with a 34-24 loss to Alabama in the first round, and Oklahoma has struggled to find consistency this year. The potent offense Oklahoma showcased last season has largely been absent throughout the 2026 campaign. The exceptions came in the season opener against UTEP, when the Sooners cruised to a 51-0 victory, and this past weekend, when they defeated then-No. 1 Texas in the Red River Rivalry. However, not all 27 points against Texas came from the offense. Oklahoma scored a touchdown after blocking and recovering a punt in the end zone, while another touchdown came on a pick-six. The Sooners’ other scoring plays included a rushing touchdown and two field goals. Across their other three games, Oklahoma has averaged just 12.3 points per game, which is disappointing for an offense expected to be productive under quarterback John Mateer. Speaking of Mateer, he has completed 90 of 135 pass attempts for a 66.7% completion rate, totaling 1,038 passing yards, eight touchdowns, and four interceptions this season. Mateer is also a running threat, recording 53 carries for 70 rushing yards. Those numbers fall short of his previous two seasons in terms of passing production. In 2025, Mateer threw for 2,885 yards, while he recorded 3,139 passing yards in 2024. His touchdown-to-interception numbers also tell an interesting story. Mateer threw 14 touchdowns and 11 interceptions in 2025, compared with 29 touchdowns and seven interceptions in 2024. For Oklahoma to defeat Kentucky, the Sooners will need Mateer to take another step forward and help their offense become more consistent. For Kentucky to win in Norman, Kenny Minchey and the offense will have to find a way to pierce the Sooners’ stingy defense and avoid game-breaking turnovers that won Oklahoma the game vs. then-No. 1 Texas. As for other notable Oklahoma players, the receiving corps features wide receiver Isaiah Sategna III, Mateer’s primary target, along with tight end Rocky Beers and wide receiver Trell Harris. Kentucky will need to account for all three playmakers while also limiting the Sooners’ running game, which features Lloyd Avant and Jonathan Hatton Jr. Game: Kentucky Football vs. Oklahoma Sooners Location: Oklahoma Memorial Stadium — Norman, Oklahoma Date: Saturday, Oct. 17 Time: 7:30 p.m. ET TV Info: SEC Network will have the TV broadcast Online Streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening Odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a 6.5-point underdog . ESPN gives Kentucky a 32.1% chance of winning. Our Early Prediction: Kentucky enters this matchup at 5-1 under first-year head coach Will Stein after a huge upset over LSU, while Oklahoma is coming off a rivalry win over Texas. Both teams could experience an emotional hangover after their big victories, but I believe Kentucky can overcome that challenge and earn another road win. Despite concerns about linebacker injuries, the Wildcats have a chance to improve to 6-1, become bowl-eligible, and remain in the College Football Playoff conversation. home.headline: Oklahoma Sooners' injury report for matchup vs. Texas Longhorns opened eyes to an issue that's been going on since 2024
home.blurb: The Oklahoma Sooners head into the Red River Rivalry against the Texas Longhorns with a long injury list. At this point, what's new? Banged-up rosters have become the norm for OU over the last few years. Ever since the SEC's player availability reports started in 2024, the Sooners have almost always carried a health disadvantage into game day. George Stoia of SoonersScoop.com pointed out a number that puts it in perspective, and I think it's worth mentioning. Stoia laid it out: OU averages 10.25 players on the initial availability report since it began in 2024. Its opponents averaged 6.68. OU has had fewer players on the initial report only once-the College Football Playoff game against Alabama. The Sooners had 6 players on that report. That feels about right. Nobody needs to stat-check it, either. Thursday's availability report for OU vs. Texas tells the same story . The Sooners have five players listed as out, two doubtful, one questionable, and five probable. Oklahoma – Out: Taylor Heim, Trell Harris, Xavier Robinson, Jacobe Johnson, Fred Hinton – Doubtful: Trynae Washington, Michael Fasusi – Questionable: Eddie Pierre-Louis – Probable: Jer'Michael Carter, Cole Sullivan, Michael Boganowski, Owen Heinecke, Jack Van Dorselaer. Texas – Out: Kaliq Lockett, Jordan Coleman, Zion Williams – Questionable: Justus Terry That's 13 names for Oklahoma and four for Texas. That's just how it is for the Sooners every week. When the Wednesday report came out, some fans were legitimately concerned. The list looked worse than it did heading into the Georgia game, even though OU had a bye week in between. More names showed up after a week off, not fewer. So fans scrambled to figure out how a team gets more injured during a bye. Fair enough, that's a decent question to ask. How does that work? I have no idea. Most likely, some players got more banged up in the Georgia game, and we just didn't know about it going into the bye. That's why building depth in the NIL era matters so much. You're going to have injuries, and OU seems to have more than anybody. Maybe that perception is right, maybe it's wrong. Regardless, the depth has to be better. You can sit here and look at this issue all you want and try to figure out what's going wrong internally. The game still has to be played. Texas isn't going to skip the Red River Rivalry because Oklahoma has a lot of guys on the report. You'd love to see the Sooners keep building their depth so the next man up can carry more of the load. For now, the Longhorns definitely have the advantage. Texas is already the No. 1-ranked team in the country, and the Sooners are coming in with really bad football. With 13 players on the availability report, OU will need its backups to step up. picks.blurb: Adam Carriker's Nebraska vs. Oregon Preview and Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska football is hitting the road for one of its biggest games of the season, and Adam Carriker is breaking it all down on the Carriker Chronicles! Matt Rhule and the Nebraska Cornhuskers are heading to Eugene to face Dan Lanning and the Oregon Ducks in a late-night Big Ten showdown. Both teams are coming off losses, and both have plenty to prove. Can the Huskers bounce back and pull off an upset? Nebraska enters the game at 5-1 after a heartbreaking loss to Curt Cignetti and Indiana. The Huskers showed some good things against the Hoosiers, but once again, they couldn't finish the job. Carriker discusses why Nebraska needs more than another moral victory. At some point, the Huskers have to start winning these big games, especially against talented Big Ten opponents. One of the biggest questions is whether Anthony Colandrea and Nebraska's offense can get things going against Oregon's defense. Colandrea has shown he can make plays, but Carriker believes offensive coordinator Dana Holgorsen needs to put him in good situations, especially on third downs. The Huskers also need production from Jamal Rule and the running back rotation. Can Nebraska establish a running game and keep Oregon's defense guessing? On the other side of the ball, Nebraska's Blackshirts face a major challenge. Oregon has talented receivers who can stretch the field and create explosive plays. Carriker looks at Nebraska's defensive numbers and explains why the Huskers cannot allow Oregon to make big plays over the top. The Blackshirts have been improving, but this will be another serious test of just how far they've come. Carriker also breaks down Oregon's defense, including players like Matayo Uiagalelei and Bear Alexander. The Ducks have plenty of talent, but Oregon has also been unpredictable this season. Nebraska cannot afford to let this become the game where everything suddenly clicks for Oregon. This is also Nebraska's stiffest road test so far this year. Playing in Eugene, in front of a loud Oregon crowd, will test the Huskers' experience and mental toughness. Nebraska has added veteran players who have been through big games before. Now it's time to see whether that experience pays off. Carriker shares his four keys to the game: handle Oregon's crowd, execute in the red zone, prevent big plays and play all four quarters. Nebraska must protect Colandrea, finish drives and avoid the mistakes that have cost the Huskers in close games. Finally, Carriker discusses the point spread and makes his score prediction! He's picking Nebraska to pull off the upset, 24-21! Can Matt Rhule and the Huskers shock Oregon, earn their third Big Ten win and make a statement to the rest of college football? Or will Dan Lanning and the Ducks send Nebraska home with another disappointing loss? Get Adam Carriker's full Nebraska-Oregon preview, breakdown and prediction on the Carriker Chronicles! picks.headline: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon
picks.blurb: 'I Will Ride or Die with Anthony Colandrea': Matt Rhule Recaps Nebraska's Loss to Indiana, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska head coach Matt Rhule knows 55 minutes of good football isn't enough. It might be against some teams, but not most. As the Huskers look to bounce back from a three-point loss to defending national champion Indiana , Rhule and his staff are making that a point of emphasis for the entire team. At the same time, Rhule is willing to bet on his quarterback to get the job done. Meeting with the media Monday, Rhule reiterated that message and shed light on the Big Red's preparations for its Week 7 road game against the Oregon Ducks. Here's everything he had to say. Anthony Colandrea looks to pass against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. NU led for much of the game Saturday afternoon, yet the Hoosiers came crawling back. Even when Indiana took the lead late in the fourth quarter, Rhule was still willing to bet on Colandrea to make a play. Asked about going for it on fourth-and-nine, the head coach pointed to what the analytics said: Go for it. It didn't work out this time, but he said he'd do it again. “I just felt like I was going to follow the analytics and put the ball in Anthony’s hands,” Rhule said. “We had holes that we thought were open and felt like, if we wanted to win that game, that ball and that field position, when you needed about 20 yards to kick a field goal, I’m going to put it in Colandrea's hands.” “I don’t always follow the analytics,” he continued. “I felt like our defense would get the stop, but more importantly, I just felt like I needed to put this ball in my guys' hands. I will ride or die with Anthony Colandrea all day, every day.” Indiana head coach Curt Cignetti and FOX Sports' Joel Klatt walk on the sideline during warmups before Saturday's game. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. There's no shame in losing to perhaps the best coach in college football in 2026. Still, Nebraska had the Hoosiers on the ropes and failed to put them away. Rhule knows the Huskers need to be better in a few key moments, like that fourth-and-nine, but he doesn't believe the team needs to overhaul much. “When we watched the tape on Sunday, I think you have a team that is angry, who knows they let one get away,” he said. “We’re certainly disappointed, but not discouraged. We also understand that that is what it looks like. You have to not play really well for 55 minutes, you have to play well for 60.” “I think each and every one of us: coaches, staff, players, knows that we have to be one or two plays better,” he continued. “I’ve encouraged the guys to take this time to be one or two plays better, every one of us, so that we can win that game when it comes back in the future.” Kyle Cunanan kicks a PAT last season. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. The offense wasn't the only unit that missed an opportunity to make a play. Nebraska's special teams failed to convert a 40-yard field goal late in the first half, a miss that proved costly in the three-point loss. Even so, Rhule still has confidence in his specialists. NU is just 3-for-7 on field-goal attempts in 2026, but the Huskers' head coach said a strong week of practice would influence his decision to trust the kicking game moving forward. “I don’t know if it was perfect, but that’s one we should make,” said Rhule. “I think we’ve had our share of issues so far… We had a missed extra point against Maryland. We had a bad snap against Maryland… I can’t live in a world of confident (or) not confident. I have to err on the side of going for it.” “If we have a great week of practice, then I’ll lean towards that (kicking),” he continued. “But with Anthony, we basically have been like, ‘Hey, we’re going to try to play four downs’. Not because we don’t trust our field goal game, but because we believe in the weapons we have on offense… But yeah, it’s just something we’ve got to get cleaned up this week before we go to Oregon.” Football out west. 🗓️ 10.17.26 ⏰ 10:00 PM CT 🏟️ Autzen Stadium vs Oregon 📺 @CFBONFOX pic.twitter.com/Cy6UNrS913 Nebraska's game at Oregon will feature the latest kickoff time Rhule has ever coached, with the game certain to extend into the early hours of Sunday morning Central time. Fleck had done, I had read some of the things that Charles Huff at Memphis had done, and a lot of it just goes into sleep,” he said. “We’re really asking our guys to go to bed a little bit later each night this week.” “We’re going to finish this game at 2 a.m. our time,” he continued. “Your circadian rhythm starts to shut down, so we’re really just trying, as best as we can, to make 2 a.m. become 12 a.m., make 12 a.m. become 10 p.m. in terms of our bodies this week.” Anthony Colandrea carries the ball against Indiana. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Having a veteran team likely helps, but so does having a quarterback who sets the tone for the entire team. picks.blurb: 'An Opportunity Missed': Nebraska Defensive Coordinator Rob Aurich Recaps Indiana Loss, Previews Oregon Skip to main content SI.COM ALL THE GAMES ALUMNI GROUPS FOOTBALL SCHEDULE SI.COM HUSKERS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM HUSKERS BB Nebraska had Indiana bottled up until they didn't. College football games last 60 minutes for a reason, and the Cornhuskers ultimately couldn't hold on to a two-possession lead in the fourth quarter. As Nebraska defensive coordinator Rob Aurich prepares his unit for a road matchup against a capable Oregon offense Saturday night, he met with the media Tuesday to recap the Blackshirts' performance against the Hoosiers and preview the challenge ahead against the nation's 25th-ranked offense. Aurich knows his defense played well for much of Saturday's game. Even so, he sees an opportunity for the Blackshirts to learn from what went wrong. “An opportunity missed,” he said. “Haunting a little bit, but don’t let the game beat you twice. You take what you can; you learn from it. First year with these guys. I think it’s an excellent opportunity for us to understand what winning time is and how we perform in those moments.” As the Huskers prepare for Oregon, they'll need to make plays in critical moments to have a chance to pull off the upset. I’m pleased where we are, but I don’t think we’re anywhere near where I think we can be still.” Oregon Ducks quarterback Dylan Raiola carries the ball against UCLA. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Oregon's running back duo of Jordan Davison and Dierre Hill won't be the only matchup for Husker Nation to watch. They’re going to have a little bit of RPO free access. The Nebraska Cornhuskers took the defending champion Indiana Hoosiers to the wire, leading for over three quarters before eventually falling 20-17 to the top five team. But sadly, it wasn't meant to be for Anthony Colandrea (pictured above, pointing to Will Compton en route to a 39-yard touchdown that put the Huskers up 17-6, seemingly icing the game for Big Red) and Company, as Herbert Hoover found Nick Marsh for two fourth-quarter scores, keeping the visitors from Bloomington unbeaten. It was, of course, Nebraska's first loss of the season. This team will go the way of its quarterback. How far can Anthony Colandrea carry the Nebraska Cornhuskers? That depends on if every defense will drop eight into coverage and rush three. Three of those eight in coverage are likely SPIES working for the enemy. Well, spies spying on our beloved quarterback. AC also had a few bad throws, struggling to feed his receivers catchable passes. For the first time this season, Nebraska did not throw a touchdown pass. The running game barely scraped by the century mark. Big plays crushed the defense. But if you looked at this game and don't see progress, you're being willfully ignorant. The Huskers controlled the ball, nearly doubling the time of possession. Nebraska was the more physical team, and the defense shut down two prominent opposing rushers. Now Big Red travels to Eugene to face the Oregon Ducks. Oregon just lost to UCLA, benched Dylan Raiola for a former walk-on, and was bumped from the Top 25. Needless to say, it's been a big week for the Ducks. Let's look at what the experts are saying. Vegas oddsmakers believe that this is a much better Nebraska team than what they predicted in the summer. Before the season, the spread for this game was 21.5 points. Immediately after the Nebraska/Indiana game, the spread was 12.5 points. Then Oregon lost to the Bruins. As of this writing, the FanDuel Sportsbook has the home Ducks as a 7.5-point favorite. The Over/Under is currently set at 52.5 points. Put the coffee on for a long night. Nebraska and Oregon kick off at 10:00pm Central Saturday night.

Nebraska Cornhuskers Have Been Competitive Against Quality Opponents Nebraska enters Saturday at 5-1 overall and 2-1 in Big Ten play after suffering its first defeat of the season. The Cornhuskers opened with five consecutive victories, including an impressive 48-23 win over Maryland, before facing undefeated Indiana on Saturday. Nebraska came close to earning a significant conference victory but ultimately fell 20-17 after Indiana completed a late comeback. The defeat was frustrating, although the Cornhuskers demonstrated enough quality to suggest they can compete against some of the conference’s stronger opponents. The performance against Indiana was particularly encouraging because Nebraska controlled several important statistical categories. The Cornhuskers generated 391 total yards compared with Indiana’s 328 and held possession for more than 39 minutes. Nebraska also ran 83 offensive plays while limiting Indiana to just 44, demonstrating an ability to control the tempo and prevent an explosive opponent from establishing sustained pressure. However, the Cornhuskers couldn’t convert that statistical advantage into enough points, allowing Indiana to remain competitive before taking the lead late. Nebraska has averaged 39.2 points per game while allowing just 15.2, numbers that reflect a team with considerable balance on both sides of the football. The Cornhuskers have also demonstrated effective rushing production, which could become particularly important against an Oregon defense that has struggled during portions of its schedule. Saturday presents a difficult road challenge at Autzen Stadium, but Nebraska’s performance against Indiana suggests the team should be capable of remaining competitive if it avoids costly mistakes. The Ducks had demonstrated impressive offensive potential during their opening stretch, but Saturday’s defeat exposed some significant concerns about their ability to maintain consistent execution against disciplined defensive opponents. Oregon struggled to generate enough scoring opportunities and couldn’t recover from several costly mistakes, allowing UCLA to secure an important conference victory. The Ducks have averaged approximately 41 points per game while allowing 22, although those numbers are heavily influenced by their earlier offensive performances. Oregon has demonstrated an ability to generate substantial production through its passing and rushing attacks, but the defeat against UCLA illustrated how quickly that offense can become ineffective when turnovers and poor situational execution interrupt drives. The Ducks also experienced difficulty establishing a consistent rushing attack, preventing them from controlling possession during important stretches. Returning to Autzen Stadium provides Oregon with an opportunity to regroup, particularly against a Nebraska team coming off its own disappointing defeat. The Ducks have demonstrated enough offensive ability to challenge quality opponents, but Nebraska’s defensive performance against Indiana suggests Saturday won’t be an easy matchup. Oregon needs to establish possession early, avoid turnovers, and prevent the Cornhuskers from controlling the clock through their rushing attack. The Ducks remain a dangerous opponent at home, but their recent offensive inconsistency makes covering a double-digit spread more challenging than their earlier performances might suggest. Nebraska also possesses a productive rushing attack capable of limiting possessions and preventing Oregon from establishing sustained momentum. The Ducks may ultimately secure the victory at Autzen Stadium, but Nebraska has demonstrated enough balance to remain competitive. The Cornhuskers are the preferred side with the points. Both defenses demonstrated the ability to contain quality offensive opponents, and both offenses experienced difficulty converting opportunities into points. Nebraska should emphasize its rushing attack and attempt to control possession, particularly after holding the football for more than 39 minutes against Indiana. Oregon possesses enough offensive ability to create explosive scoring opportunities, but the Ducks may approach this matchup more cautiously after their mistakes against UCLA. away.headline: Nebraska's lineup is taking shape of exhibition play, but Orme's injury looms
Oregon's Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola, an Injury and a Brock Thomas QB Competition for Nebraska
away.blurb: But at Autzen Stadium, one QB is going to run out for the first offensive snap for the Ducks, and no matter who it is, it'll be a fascinating decision. Oregon's Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola, an Injury and a Brock Thomas QB Competition for Nebraska The Oregon Ducks are home on Saturday night to host the Nebraska Cornhuskers. For those tuned in to these two teams, there are a lot of narratives at play — and many of them stem from the Ducks' QB depth chart of Dante Moore, Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas. It's the kind of situation that may or may not get more clarity before kickoff on Saturday. Is Dante Moore Playing This Week? The intrigue starts with Moore, whose playing status for the game against Nebraska seems to remain uncertain. He hasn't played since being concussed against USC on a dirty hit after he slid to the turf. Raiola replaced him in that game, then the Ducks had a bye, and then Raiola started last week. Whether or not Moore will miss another game is a crucial factor one way or the other, but it doesn't seem decided. Is Dylan Raiola Starting This Week? The next factor at play is Raiola, who was pulled midway through Oregon's loss to UCLA. He was just 6-for-19 for 43 yards with two interceptions before head coach Dan Lanning pulled him in the fourth quarter. Lanning told reporters at the start of this week that if Moore can't go on Saturday, that will bring about a QB competition in practice for who starts against the Cornhuskers. Of course, Raiola would love to face Nebraska. That's the school he played at for two years after being the No. 1 quarterback recruit in the country. Then he transferred to Oregon in the offseason, and it seemed he'd just be the backup when the Ducks played the Cornhuskers — but now there's at least a chance he starts. Thomas began the year as Oregon's third quarterback, but he went 11-for-15 for 156 yards and a touchdown in an attempted comeback against UCLA. He's not the high-pedigree recruit of the Ducks' other two quarterbacks, but sometimes productivity gets rewarded. Thomas is actually a cool story, because he's from Eugene and played locally at Sheldon High School. He played in a state title game in high school and also won a 4×100-meter relay state title on the track. A three-star recruit, Thomas picked the hometown team as a third-generation Ducks player — his grandfather Paul Bauge and father Aaron Thomas both played at Oregon, too. home.blurb: Oregon's Dan Lanning reached out after Nico Iamaleava's injury - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Oregon's Dan Lanning reached out after Nico Iamaleava's injury There's not too much love lost between the Oregon Ducks and the UCLA Bruins . The two schools have been conference rivals for over 50 years but that doesn't mean that they can't look out for one another. A few weeks back, Oregon quarterback Dante Moore was injured in Los Angeles after taking a hit to the head in a game against USC. Following the game, UCLA head coach Bob Chesney reached out to Oregon head coach Dan Lanning to see if he could provide any aid to Moore. This article originally appeared on UCLA Wire: Oregon's Dan Lanning reached out after Nico Iamaleava's injury Dylan McNeill, UCLA Wire Wed, October 14, 2026 at 2:01 PM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Moore ended up traveling back to Oregon with the team, ultimately not needing any assistance from Chesney. Lanning returned the favor this week, contacting Chesney after UCLA's quarterback, Nico Iamaleava, went down with an injury on Saturday . During Tuesday's media availability , Chesney made it clear that he was appreciative while adding some details. "I think he's stand-up as a man and as a football coach as you possibly can be. He not only called me about Nico, but he also called me when we were in the hotel when our plane was delayed," Chesney said. "He was like 'Is there anything we can help with? Do you need a place to go?' Just that type of person." To add onto Iamaleava's injury, he was also struck in the face by an Oregon defender during the play. Both coaches have spoken about the alleged punch but it's clear that there's no bad blood between the two Big Ten Conference coaches.

home.headline: Why isn’t Dante Moore playing for Oregon against UCLA? The Ducks QB’s injury status
home.blurb: Moore returned to practice this week, but he remains in concussion protocol and was officially listed as out on Oregon’s availability report. The Ducks are taking a cautious approach to his recovery, with no timetable announced for his return. Moore returned to practice on Monday, October 5 , following Oregon’s bye week. His return was an encouraging development, but it did not mean he was ready to play. Lanning said the Ducks would continue to prioritize what was best for Moore as he worked through the recovery process. Moore remained in concussion protocol and was ruled out for the UCLA game on the conference’s availability report released Wednesday. The quarterback must complete the necessary steps in the concussion protocol before he can return to game action. Oregon has not announced a target date for his comeback. With Moore unavailable, Dylan Raiola is set to make his first start for Oregon . The former Nebraska quarterback replaced Moore against USC and helped the Ducks secure the victory, completing 19 of 25 passes for 289 yards and two touchdowns . “He had an expectation when he stepped out there on the field and performed at a really, really high level, and everybody had confidence in him because they see him do it a lot in practice, ” Lanning said. What injury does Dante Moore have? Moore suffered a concussion during Oregon’s 41-27 victory over USC on September 26. home.blurb: Oregon QB Dante Moore out for No. 13 Ducks against No. 21 UCLA after head injury; Dylan Raiola to start - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF Moore was listed as out on Oregon's initial injury report Wednesday night. He had returned to practice on Monday, according to coach Dan Lanning. Moore was considered a potential top-two pick in the 2026 NFL Draft before he decided to return to school. His decision came after Raiola committed to Oregon following two seasons with the Cornhuskers. Nick Bromberg Senior writer Thu, October 8, 2026 at 12:11 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads In this story No. 13 Oregon won't have Dante Moore for its game against No. 21 UCLA on Saturday. Moore suffered a concussion in the Ducks' Week 4 win over USC when his head violently hit the turf following a helmet-to-helmet hit while sliding. USC LB Desman Stephens II was ejected for targeting on the play and subsequently suspended for USC's Week 5 win over Washington for his actions after the play. With Moore unable to go, former Nebraska quarterback Dylan Raiola will get his first start in an Oregon uniform. Raiola replaced Moore against the Trojans and was 19-of-25 passing for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the 41-27 victory. The Ducks were off in Week 5. Through portions of four games, Moore is 69-of-99 passing for 926 yards and nine touchdowns with no interceptions, while Raiola has thrown for 413 yards on 36 pass attempts after attempting his first throws of the season in Oregon's win over Portland State in Week 3.
